CHIEF COMPLAINT
Recurrent kidney stone with history of hypertension and diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with recurrent kidney stones. Pain has been intermittent. Patient went to the emergency room last week and believes the stone passed approximately three days ago. Denies current blood in urine and denies current pain. States this is approximately her seventh or eighth kidney stone. Emergency room staff provided pain medication (Percocet). Patient has not seen a urologist in approximately one year but has been evaluated in the past for recurrent kidney stones.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Denies current flank pain. Patient reports occasional insomnia with worry as a contributing factor. Reports that meditation apps have been somewhat helpful. Has tried melatonin a couple of times with minimal benefit. Patient sleeps with television on and keeps phone at bedside. Denies proper sleep hygiene practices.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus type 2
Recurrent kidney stones (approximately 7-8 episodes)
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known, unchanged)
Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports fast food consumption and difficulty modifying diet due to time constraints and on-the-go lifestyle. Lives a busy lifestyle with limited time for meal preparation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 150/90 mmHg at visit (home readings 130-140/60-70 mmHg). Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles. Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from previous exam. Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angle: No tenderness bilaterally.

RESULTS
A1C from last visit: 6.7% (patient has not been regularly checking home blood glucose).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Recurrent kidney stones: Stones appear to have passed. Obtain urinalysis and urine culture to ensure resolution. Referral to urology with Dr. Harris for evaluation and management of recurrent kidney stones.
Hypertension: Blood pressure control adequate on current regimen. Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. No medication changes needed. Discussed possible white coat syndrome. Continue home blood pressure monitoring 2-3 times weekly.
Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient instructed to check blood glucose before each meal to better assess dietary intake. Referral to nutrition consultation for dietary modification and sodium restriction (goal <2300 mg sodium daily).
Insomnia: Start melatonin 10 mg as needed. Counseled on sleep hygiene practices including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and using iPhone sleep mode to minimize disturbances. Patient declined prescription sleep medications.
Follow-up: Return visit in 3 months.
